evaluationStatus: POST_EVALUATION, NOT BLIND: decisions were made after seeing question, options, key, frozen model label, frozen linter emissions and why the case mattered. Not held-out evidence for these 13 cases.

decisions.humanReasoning: The Hebrew "שלא" is relative/content negation inside the physical condition. The question does not ask the learner to select what is NOT true or perform negative-stem reasoning.
decisions.humanRule: Negation token != negative-stem flaw. Content/relative negation is not sufficient.

before.label: FLAWED
before.semanticExpectation: Stem names the distractor category ('ולא לכלי כתיבה'), giving away that עט/עיפרון are the excluded options; the contrast phrasing is a cue.

semanticDecision.concern: semantic cue concern (stem names the excluded category)

decisions.humanReasoning: "ולא" expresses natural category contrast. It is not negative-stem reasoning. Explicitly distinguishing musical instruments from writing tools defines the classification task; it does not by itself leak the key.
decisions.humanRule: Contrast wording != negative-stem flaw. Explicit category contrast != cue by itself.

before.label: FLAWED
before.semanticExpectation: Stem 'מימי הביניים' is a bare noun phrase.

decisions.humanReasoning: "מימי הביניים" is a noun-phrase fragment rather than a well-formed question. The key is also strongly isolated by length and specificity relative to the three short distractors.
decisions.humanRule: Length alone is not always a flaw, but strong isolated length + specificity asymmetry can create a real test-taking cue.

decisions.humanReasoning: "מהם גזי חממה?" is a valid complete short Hebrew question. "כל האפשרויות הנ\"ל" is clearly an all-of-the-above option.
decisions.humanRule: Valid Hebrew interrogative morphology must not be rejected merely because the stem has fewer than four words. Also record: מה / מהו / מהי / מהם / מהן are members of the same broad interrogative family for future design consideration (NOT implemented in this Run).
decisions.designNote: Future design consideration only, NOT implemented in this Run: מה / מהו / מהי / מהם / מהן are members of the same broad interrogative family.

before.label: FLAWED
before.semanticExpectation: Stem 'במה' is a single ambiguous word (in what / stage) and not a well-formed question; options mix homographs.

decisions.humanReasoning: "במה" alone is ambiguous/incomplete. It can lexically represent either a noun ("stage") or an interrogative form, but by itself it does not form a sufficiently well-defined question here.
decisions.humanRule: Morphological ability to be interrogative is not sufficient for short-stem exemption. The complete utterance must function as a clear question/instruction.

before.label: FLAWED
before.semanticExpectation: Stem 'שמי הלילה' is a bare noun phrase; 'שמי' only resembles a prefixed interrogative.

decisions.humanReasoning: "שמי הלילה" is a noun phrase, not a question. The current prefix mechanism falsely treats its first word as interrogative-like.
decisions.humanRule: Morphological resemblance alone must not exempt a short stem.

before.label: FLAWED
before.semanticExpectation: Stem 'List of birds' is a noun phrase, not a question, despite the imperative-looking first word.

decisions.humanReasoning: "List of birds" is a noun phrase / label in this context, not a complete imperative. The fact that "List" can be a command verb is insufficient.
decisions.humanRule: A lead word that can begin an imperative does not automatically make the entire short stem well-formed.

before.label: FLAWED
before.semanticExpectation: Stem 'Name tags' is a noun phrase; 'Name' looks imperative but nothing is asked.

decisions.humanReasoning: "Name tags" is a noun phrase. "Name" can be an imperative verb in other contexts, but is not functioning as one here.
decisions.humanRule: Lexical form alone is insufficient for short-stem exemption.

before.label: FLAWED
before.semanticExpectation: Stem already defines proportional representation ('מנדטים מחולקים לפי חלקן ... בקולות') and key c merely restates it (circular; stem leaks the key).

semanticDecision.concern: semantic stem/key leakage concern; no deterministic code expected

decisions.humanReasoning: The key naturally restates the definition supplied by the stem. Semantic overlap in a definition question is not itself leakage.
decisions.humanRule: Restating the concept defined by the stem is not automatically leakage. Leakage requires an asymmetric cue that can identify the key without the intended knowledge.

before.label: FLAWED
before.semanticExpectation: Key 'Merge sort' echoes the stem verb 'merges' (name leak); borderline since the name is the standard term.

semanticDecision.concern: semantic leakage concern; no deterministic code expected

decisions.humanReasoning: "Merge sort" naturally shares vocabulary with the defining operation "merges". This is the standard technical term, not an unfair cue by itself.
decisions.humanRule: A standard term sharing vocabulary with its defining behavior is not leakage by itself.

before.label: FLAWED
before.semanticExpectation: Key c restates the stem phrase 'תופעת הגאות והשפל' and is the longest option: self-referential key echoing the stem (lexical leakage).

semanticDecision.concern: semantic stem-key leakage (key uniquely repeats distinctive stem phrase "תופעת הגאות והשפל")

decisions.humanReasoning: The key is materially longer and more specific than the distractors. Separately, it uniquely repeats the distinctive stem phrase "תופעת הגאות והשפל", creating asymmetric stem-key echo.
decisions.humanRule: Stem-key echo is a real defect when the key uniquely mirrors distinctive stem wording in a way the distractors do not. IMPORTANT: this does NOT authorize restoring broad deterministic KEY_STEM_LEXICAL_OVERLAP.
decisions.humanNotes: Does NOT authorize restoring broad deterministic KEY_STEM_LEXICAL_OVERLAP.

decisions.humanReasoning: "בהכרח" is semantically part of the misconception claim, but its strong, asymmetric absolute wording also makes the distractor easier to reject.
decisions.humanRule: Strong absolute wording can be a valid warning when it appears asymmetrically in a distractor, even where it is also part of misconception content.

before.label: FLAWED
before.semanticExpectation: Distractor b is implausible and recycles the stem's own term ('התחממות גלובלית ... קרינת הירח'), and d uses the exclusive 'בלבד'; weak distractors with a circular option.

semanticDecision.decision: APPROVED / REAL_DEFECT (weak-distractor/implausibility); weak-tier "בלבד" cue APPROVED AS CONTEXTUAL SEMANTIC CONCERN
semanticDecision.concern: distractor b implausible/circular and weak; "בלבד" further weakens distractor d in context

decisions.humanReasoning: Distractor b is implausible/circular and weak. "בלבד" further weakens distractor d in context, but the token alone is not sufficient for deterministic ownership.
decisions.humanRule: Weak absolute terms can contribute to a cue, but the flaw is contextual. Weak-tier tokens alone remain semantic/human territory.
decisions.humanNotes: OPTION_ABSOLUTE_TERM has NO deterministic expectation for this case (weak-tier token alone is semantic/human territory); semanticExpectation retained as the approved contextual concern.
